title: 21st Sitting of third session of 2025
presiding: Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Speaker), then Ahmed Nazim (Deputy Speaker) after the 10:31-11:02 recess
summary: The 21st sitting opened at 9:02 on 18 November 2025 and went straight into the continuing debate on the government's proposed 2026 state budget (about MVR 64.2 billion, of which around MVR 55 billion is for repaying past debt). Most members who spoke backed the budget and listed projects for their islands, while the members for Meedhoo and North Hulhumale' questioned spending on regional airports, embassies, company subsidies and Hulhumale' service fees. Finance Minister Moosa Zameer replied twice, saying 2026 is the year of the largest debt repayments in the country's history; his second reply was still under way when this part ends. No votes were held in this part, and the text is garbled in places so the attendance count could not be read reliably. This part continues the debate on the government's proposed 2026 state budget of about MVR 64.2 billion. After a minister finished replying to earlier points, eight members spoke: MDP members (Thoddoo, South Hithadhoo, Keyodhoo) criticised rising spending, borrowing and missing detail, while government-side members backed the budget and listed island projects. The chair closed the debate after 60 members had spoken in total, noted that the Finance Minister had answered in writing, and said members' views would go to the budget review committee. The sitting was adjourned to 19 November 2025 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places, but speakers and the closing procedure are clear.

items.title: Debate on the proposed 2026 state budget (Rule 235 of the Majlis rules)
items.outcome: debated; closed after 60 members spoke in total; views to be passed to the budget review committee; no vote in this part

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Backed the 2026 budget and listed Dhidhdhoo projects: an airport, hospital, football ground and sports facilities.
Said past governments left the country in a weak state and that the president's pledges on drugs, migrant workers and housing are being delivered with this budget.

speakers.name: Moosa Zameer
positions: Said 2026 is the year of the largest debt repayments in the country's history, so the budget was prepared around that with no new fees or higher charges.
Said the government wants to widen the tax base through more businesses and merge regional airports under MACL, and described plans to repay or roll over about USD 600 million due.
Began replying to members on debt sustainability, repayment mechanisms and tax collection patterns; the reply continues past this part.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Asked whether the state should run a service company for Hulhumale' instead of leaving services to HDC, and raised residents' complaints about lift and maintenance fees.
Called for more help for single mothers and social protection, and for jobs for Maldivians in place of reliance on foreign workers.
Welcomed pay harmonisation and a controlled budget but warned that refinancing debt and paying only interest year after year is not good.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Raised a point of order saying the budget has no project for any island and that the Dhidhdhoo member's claim was false; the chair did not treat it as a point of order.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Supported the budget, noting about MVR 55 billion of the MVR 64.2 billion goes to debt repayment, and listed allocations for health, defence and education.
Asked members to consider that the human rights and family protection bodies received less than before.
Raised Nilandhoo's power, water and sea-erosion problems and asked the government to speed up solutions.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Backed the budget and listed its fiscal targets: deficit below 5% of GDP by 2028, debt cut toward 117% of GDP, interest below 12% of revenue.
Said the deficit falls from 10.5% to 5.5% and that health receives the largest share, with MVR 8.3 billion for development projects.
Welcomed work on the Vilifushi airport and projects in his islands.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: Thanked the government and listed budget items for Gemanafushi and nearby islands: sewerage, harbours, roads, a police station, an ATM and a football ground.
Said the budget addresses fishers' problems in Huvadhu atoll, citing cold storage at Kooddoo and a fish factory at Fiyoaree.
Said the government has reclaimed and handed out record amounts of land and housing, countering claims by the opposition.

speakers.name: Ahmed Siyam Mohamed
positions: Said the main test of a record budget is spending wisely, and warned that high interest rates, low reserves and large pay rises could drive inflation.
Questioned spending on regional airports, foreign embassies and subsidies to all state companies, saying returns should guide investment.
Called for Maldivians to hold more ownership of tourism businesses and asked the minister to cut spending where possible.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Said the government inherited a weak economy, bankrupt companies and unfinished projects, such as classrooms and a hospital lacking required facilities.
Described Maafushi as a major tourism island and asked for water, sewerage, roads and a hospital that fits its population.
Called 2026 a budget of hope and said promised items for Maafushi are being fulfilled.

speakers.name: Ali Ashrag
positions: Backed the budget's targets: deficit below 5% of GDP, debt cut to 117% of GDP, development spending at or below 7% and interest below 12% of revenue.
Said projects in Vandhoo, Kandoodhoo, Hirilandhoo, Omadhoo and Kinbidhoo can proceed under the budget without funding trouble.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Called the MVR 64.2 billion budget the largest ever but lacking planning, and questioned spending on embassies, ministers' travel and rising debt.
Said Thoddoo's utility tariffs and green tax burden islanders, and asked why civil service hiring of 8,000 was budgeted in an election year.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aslam
positions: Supported the budget and asked for a futsal ground, roads, harbour work and the Magoodhoo airport for Faafu islands.
Backed action against corruption and asked the Finance Minister to give the budget book to opposition members too.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the budget lacks detail and that financing MVR 26.3 billion by borrowing is unrealistic, with debt rising each year.
Raised Aasandha medical welfare problems, such as medicines not covered, and asked what the extra spending delivers for ordinary people.

speakers.name: Adam Zahir
positions: Supported the budget but asked for debt risk assessments and global-conditions analysis to be shared with the House.
Said claims that islands' projects are missing from the budget mislead the public, citing the Felidhoo harbour.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Said debt rose by about MVR 35 billion in two years and recurrent spending grew while income did not.
Listed unfulfilled promises in Keyodhoo and Rakeedhoo, including health centres, a school building and sports facilities, and said the budget has no clear plan.

speakers.name: Ismail Shafeeu
positions: Fully supported the budget and listed projects for his islands, including an ice plant at Maabaidhoo and shore protection.
Welcomed upgrading the Isdhoo-Kalaidhoo road, a hospital and airport plans, and island leasing for tourism.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Said the budget aims to cut the deficit to about five percent and defended the airport and tourism growth.
Described energy, fisheries, health and sports projects for his constituency and acknowledged some delays.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the budget, saying it funds basic services, and argued opposition criticism ignores debt inherited from earlier governments.
Listed projects for Himandhoo, Maalhos, Feridhoo and Mathiveri, including health centres, a school and an airport.

decisions: The chair did not treat the Velidhoo member's point as a point of order and asked the Dhidhdhoo member to continue.
The chair called a recess from 10:31 to 11:02; the debate then resumed under the Deputy Speaker.
The budget debate was closed after 60 members had spoken in total.
Members' views on the budget will be passed to the budget review committee, and the Finance Minister's written reply was noted.
The next sitting was set for Wednesday 19 November 2025 at 9:00.
